Class RcxRemote

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.lego.RcxRemote
public final class RcxRemote extends Object
The LEGO Mindstorms RCX infrared protocol, recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno: receives the button state of an RCX Remote Control (9709) and transmits the same remote-control and message commands to an RCX brick. It is plain Java on top of Infrared, which carries the 2400 baud bytes; see there for the wiring of the IR receiver module and the IR LED. For the Scout brick, see ScoutRemote.

Every message is 55 FF 00 followed by each byte and its complement: the opcode, its arguments and a checksum. The remote sends opcode 0xD2 with a 16-bit button mask, repeatedly while a button is held and once more with the mask 0 on release.

The mask goes on the wire high byte first (D2 hh ll); the button values match the bit assignments of the NXC RCX_Remote* constants once their bytes are swapped back.

Receiving and sending are blocking: a frame takes about 50 ms at 2400 baud, during which buttons() (or message()) decodes it. Call them regularly from the main loop, not while Delay.millis is waiting. Works on both boards.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public static void begin(int receivePin, int transmitPin)
      Configures the pins: receivePin for an IR receiver module and transmitPin for an IR LED, either -1 when unused.

    • buttons

      public static int buttons()
      The buttons currently held on the remote as a mask of the button constants, or 0 when none is held. Decodes a frame if one is arriving; the last state is kept for 300 ms and then counts as released, in case the release message was missed.

    • message

      public static int message()
      The value of the most recent RCX message command (opcode 0xF7, e.g. sent by another RCX or by sendMessage(int)), 0..255, or -1 if none has arrived since the last call.

      public static void sendButtons(int buttonMask)

      Transmits an RCX message command carrying the low 8 bits of value.
